inbox.bulkHint: The decision applies to each selected task you may decide; the others are reported back.
inbox.cancelOwnHint: Withdraw your request; nobody can decide it afterwards.
inbox.cancelOtherHint: You may cancel this task as its assignee, an escalation role or an administrator.
inbox.cancelReasonHint: The reason is kept in the task history.
inbox.allClearHint: Approvals and follow-ups you can decide appear here. Tasks waiting for someone else are behind “Only what I can decide”.
inbox.emptyHint: Try another status or task type, or clear the filters.
inbox.reasonRequiredFor: Required to {{decisions}}; recorded in the audit trail.
inbox.commentPlaceholder: Add a comment for the requester or the next reviewer

check.fourEyesOwn: You requested it; a second person has to decide

criteria.jsonHint: Edit the criterion as JSON; it is applied when the field loses focus.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.deliveryDateHint: Resolves vintage and device age rules
inventory.asOfHint: The lot as it was effective at a time, as recorded at another (bitemporal).
inventory.splitHint: Of {{quantity}}; the rest stays in a second lot.
inventory.cancelHint: Cancels the certificates for a consumer; the registry instruction is created separately.
inventory.withdrawHint: Removes the lot from inventory, e.g. after a registry correction. It cannot be undone here.

purposes.ON_BEHALF_OF_THIRD_PARTY: On behalf of a third party

inventory.allowancesHint: Allowance balances by registry account. Choose a holding to see its movements and to preselect it for a movement or a transfer.

ops.reserveHint: Earmarks the certificates so that allocation and transfers leave them alone. A part of the lot is split off first.
ops.releaseHint: Releases reservation {{ref}}; the certificates become free for allocation and transfers again. If an allocation plan made it, the plan no longer holds them.
ops.correctHint: Corrects what a registry may correct in place: expiry, support, labels and cost. Other attributes need a replacement lot.

receive.title: Receive certificates
receive.hint: Records certificates in one of the entity's GoO accounts as a new lot: an issuance, a transfer in or an opening balance.
receive.unknownDevice: This GSRN is not in the device register. Describe the device so the lot can be classified.
receive.expiryHint: Empty: twelve months after the production period

movement.title: Record movement
movement.hint: Books a movement on an allowance holding. Transfers the registry executes are sent as registry instructions instead.

ladder.title: Expiry ladder
ladder.hint: Held and reserved MWh by month of expiry, next {{months}} months

journal.title: Lot journal check
journal.hint: Recomputes the hash chain of every lot's journal. A broken chain means an event was changed outside the application.
journal.intact: Every lot's journal chain is intact.
journal.broken: These lots' journal chains do not verify

kpi.expiring30Hint: Sell, allocate or cancel these first

inventory.emptyLotsHint: No lot matches the status and expiry filters.
inventory.emptyLotsAction: Received certificates appear here once they are booked.
inventory.criteriaHint: Finds the lots whose attributes meet the criteria, the way allocation matches them.

trades.title: Trades
trades.searchHint: Trade number, external ref or UTI
trades.captured: Trade {{number}} captured; it waits for approval
trades.confirmHint: Records the counterparty's confirmation; delivery obligations open once confirmed.
trades.noValuation: No official valuation for this trade on that date.

mtm.asOfHint: Results of the official run of that day

form.reasonHint: Recorded with the new version and shown to the approver.
form.amendHint: An amendment creates a new version; approved trades go back for approval.
form.newHint: Captured trades go to middle office for approval (four eyes).
form.counterpartyAccountHint: Needed before a sale can be confirmed
form.brokerHint: Optional; the broker fee follows its agreement
form.masterAgreementHint: Reference of the agreement the trade falls under
form.mirrorBookHint: Book of the other own entity; its mirror trade is captured with this one
form.futureCounterparty: Futures trade with an exchange or clearing house
form.futureDelivery: Delivers once on {{date}}, in whole lots of {{size}} t
form.futureChooseContract: Choose the contract: it sets the product, currency and delivery date
form.optionTermsHint: A European option on a futures contract. Exercise at expiry creates the future at the strike.
form.underlyingChoose: Choose the future the option is on: it sets the product and currency
form.underlyingHint: Last trading day {{day}}, whole lots of {{size}} t
form.premiumHint: Paid in full on the option; quantity is tonnes of the underlying
form.optionNoDelivery: An option delivers nothing: exercise at expiry creates the future, which delivers.
form.whatHint: The product, the instrument and when it was traded.
form.whoHint: Our book, the counterparty and, when one was used, the broker and the agreement.
form.criteriaHint: Which certificates qualify; allocation picks lots that match.
form.accountsHint: Our registry account, and the counterparty's account for a sale.
form.deliveriesHint: Each delivery: its production window, the delivery date and the quantity.
form.newLead: Capture a GoO or EUA trade. It goes to middle office for approval.
form.amendLead: Change the terms. The amendment becomes a new version of the trade.

optionTerms.noDeliveries: An option has no delivery schedule: exercise at expiry creates the future, which delivers.

ops.checkLimitsHint: Runs the pre-trade checks again against today's limits and exposures. Nothing is stored.
ops.recordHint: Records a delivery made outside the registry flows. Use the registry instructions where they apply.
ops.deliverAllowancesHint: Submits the Union Registry transfer of {{product}} for {{trade}} to the counterparty's account. The delivery is recorded when the registry confirms it.
ops.matchAllowanceHint: Choose the incoming allowance movement that delivers this purchase.
ops.matchLotHint: Choose the received lot that delivers this purchase.
ops.noDocuments: No documents yet: issue our confirmation to create one.
ops.noObligationsHint: Confirmed trades open their deliveries here, earliest first.

kpi.lastWeekHint: Trades captured since a week ago

trades.emptyHint: Captured trades appear here, newest first.
trades.emptyFilteredHint: Change or clear the filters to see the rest of the blotter.
trades.cancelHint: The trade and its open deliveries are cancelled. The reason is kept in its history.
trades.confirmationsHint: Our confirmations and the counterparty's, matched field by field.
trades.noConfirmationsHint: Issue our confirmation, then enter the counterparty's when it arrives.
trades.noValuationHint: Choose another date, or wait for the official valuation run of this one.

headroom.joint: Each delivery fits on its own, but together they ask for {{requested}} and the same certificates can serve {{mwh}}.

allocation.title: Allocation workbench
allocation.description: Open delivery obligations of {{entity}} and the certificates that cover them.
allocation.proposed: Plan proposed; it waits for a second person's approval
allocation.shortfall: {{mwh}} MWh cannot be covered with the certificates held
allocation.unpricedBadgeHint: The sale has no priced product bucket; it is valued at zero

value.title: Value

hints.deliveredValue: What the delivered certificates are worth

value.unpriced: go to sales without a priced product. They are valued at zero, so the cost and give-away figures understate them.
value.giveAwayHint: The premium handed over when a certificate worth more than the sale's own product delivers it, largest first.

shadow.title: Shadow prices
shadow.indicative: Indicative only: computed by a linear program in floating point, not unique when the program is degenerate, and never booked.

hints.lpCost: Cheapest cost of the same coverage
hints.gap: What better lot choices could still save

shadow.obligationsHint: What one more MWh delivered to the sale would cost, including rerouting other sales, highest first.
shadow.supplyHint: How much the plan's cost would fall with one more MWh of that supply, highest first.
shadow.shortHint: The sale is not fully covered; its marginal MWh may not be available at all

allocation.planTitleFuture: Plan for {{mwh}} MWh held and {{future}} MWh to come
allocation.fallback: The exact solver was not used: {{reason}}. The plan comes from the greedy solver.
allocation.openObligationHint: A disclosure or own-consumption need, or a sale delivered outside a trade. Allocation serves it like any other obligation.
allocation.priorityHint: Lower is served first; empty uses the kind's default

purposes.ON_BEHALF_OF_THIRD_PARTY: On behalf of a third party

allocation.constraintsHint: Limit how much of the obligation one production device may supply, and require a minimum share of certificates that match a criterion.
allocation.closeHint: Closing takes the remaining {{mwh}} MWh out of allocation; plans that include it become stale. What was delivered stays.
allocation.closeHintTrade: Closing takes the remaining {{mwh}} MWh of trade {{trade}} out of allocation; plans that include it become stale. If the delivery itself changed, amend or cancel the trade instead.

errors.quantity: Enter a whole number of MWh above zero
errors.window: The window must end after it starts
errors.target: A sale needs a target account
errors.percent: Enter a whole percentage from 1 to 100

allocation.coverageHint: Covered and short MWh, by target account and delivery date
allocation.noObligationsHint: Confirmed sales open obligations; disclosures and own use are opened here.
allocation.noPlansHint: Run a what if, then propose a plan for a second person to approve.
allocation.shortfallHint: Not coverable with the certificates held
allocation.planLead: Proposed by {{by}} on {{at}} with the {{solver}} solver
allocation.cancelHint: Releases the soft reservation of the plan's certificates. The reason is kept with the plan.

virtual.title: Virtual lines
virtual.note: Virtual lines are not reserved or instructed. Each one says which purchase or expected issuance would serve an obligation, and from when. Planned means the plan still counts on what it was made with; changed means the purchase or forecast it counts on has changed since the plan was made, so the line may no longer hold.

positions.title: Positions
positions.description: Coverage, expiry and compliance position of {{entity}}.
positions.noSnapshotsHint: Snapshots are taken every evening; take one now to record the current position.

kpi.shortfall: Buy or allocate to close it

portfolio.lead: Every product bucket with the buckets it sits inside: what the entity holds, what it owes that only this bucket's certificates can serve, and what is left once the two are matched by eligibility. A bucket that belongs to several larger ones is listed under each.
portfolio.note: Figures are in MWh, all vintages together; marks and cheapest to deliver are for the current vintage. Naive net is long minus short without looking at which certificates qualify; the netted columns do.
portfolio.shortHint: Open obligations that only certificates inside this bucket can serve.
portfolio.coveredWithinHint: How much of the short the bucket's own certificates can cover, matching each certificate only to obligations it qualifies for.
portfolio.shortAfterNettingHint: Short minus covered within: what must still be bought or issued.
portfolio.naiveNetHint: Long minus short, ignoring which certificates qualify. Netted means matched by eligibility: a bucket can look long here and still be short after netting when its certificates are the wrong kind.
portfolio.naiveNetMisleading: Looks long, but the bucket is short after netting: its certificates do not qualify for these obligations.
portfolio.freeHint: Certificates in the bucket that no obligation uses.
portfolio.availableToSellHint: What a new sale of exactly this product could still receive.
portfolio.markHint: The bucket's mark for the current vintage.
portfolio.cheapestToDeliverHint: The lowest value among the bucket's free certificates.
portfolio.giveAwayHint: Cheapest to deliver minus mark. A management figure; it is never booked.
portfolio.alsoUnderHint: This product sits inside several larger ones. It is listed first under {{name}}; the figures are the same here.
portfolio.emptyHint: The portfolio is worked out from the product buckets and the certificates and obligations of the entity.

futureHint.CONTRACTED: Purchases agreed but not yet delivered, inside this bucket. Added to long in the naive net.
futureHint.EXPECTED: Purchases not yet delivered and issuance expected, inside this bucket. Added to long in the naive net.

headroom.title: Available to sell
headroom.lead: The most a new sale could receive from the certificates held, per bucket and vintage, for each delivery month-end, without taking anything from sales already agreed. Existing sales may be moved onto other certificates that serve them too.
headroom.note: An upper bound: the cells share supply and do not add up, and device caps and minimum shares of existing sales are not in it.
headroom.emptyHint: Available to sell is worked out from the certificates the entity holds.

futureHint.CONTRACTED: Purchases agreed but not yet delivered that count towards this bucket and vintage.
futureHint.EXPECTED: Purchases not yet delivered and issuance expected from devices that count towards this bucket and vintage.

hint.CONTRACTED: Counts the certificates held plus purchases agreed but not yet delivered.
hint.EXPECTED: Counts the certificates held, purchases agreed but not yet delivered, and issuance expected from production devices. Expected issuance is an estimate.

future.lead: What the entity will have beyond its holdings, by delivery month: purchases agreed but not yet delivered, and certificates expected from production devices, set against the obligations due.
future.note: Neither is held yet, so none of it is reserved or can be instructed. Expected issuance is an estimate (P50); the P90 column is the cautious figure.
future.p90Hint: The quantity in MWh that production should reach in nine cases out of ten.
future.noItemsHint: There are no purchases awaiting delivery and no forecast production from the entity's devices.
future.emptyHint: Future supply appears when the entity has obligations to cover, purchases not yet delivered or devices with expected production.

marketData.title: Market data
marketData.description: Quotes, FX rates and instruments; prices are read from here by valuation, allocation and accounting.
marketData.quoteSuspect: Quote recorded but flagged as suspect; review it
marketData.pickInstrument: Pick an instrument to see its quotes
marketData.duplicate: This file was imported before; nothing changed.
marketData.tenorHint: Optional: ON, or a number with D, W, M or Y (3M, 10Y). Places a rate on a discount curve.
marketData.aliasHint: Maps a source's own code to an instrument, so imports from that source find it.
marketData.formatHint: kind is FX_WIDE_CSV, FX_ECB_XML or QUOTES_LONG_CSV; columnMapping maps fields to the file's columns and constants fill fields the file does not have.
marketData.noIndicesHint: An index fixes a price from an instrument's quotes, for indexed trades.
marketData.noFixingHint: The index has no usable quote for this date.

errors.decimal: Enter a number, with a dot for decimals
errors.tenor: Enter ON, or a number followed by D, W, M or Y (for example 3M)

marketData.pickInstrumentHint: Quotes come from imports, the ECB feed or are recorded by hand; each is checked for plausibility.

kpi.suspectHint: Review and acknowledge or replace them
kpi.instrumentsHint: Spot, futures, vintages, indices and rates
kpi.curvesHint: Snapshots are signed off by a second person

curves.title: Curves
curves.description: Snapshots of forward, vintage, discount and volatility curves; official ones are signed off by a second person.
curves.noSnapshots: No snapshot for this curve and date
curves.dayCountHint: How days between dates become years. Leave empty for the default.
curves.discountCurveInfo: Discount curve for {{currency}}, zero rates in percent a year by tenor, day count {{dayCount}}.
curves.interpolationHelp: Applies to snapshots built from now on; signed-off snapshots keep their method.

interpolations.CARRY: Grow at the last carry rate

curves.proxyHint: Fills pillars this curve has no quotes for
curves.noOfficial: No official curve on this date
curves.noOfficialHint: Build a snapshot and have it signed off, or pick another date.
curves.priceLookupHint: The price valuation uses: the latest official curve on or before the date.
curves.noDiscountCurveHint: Valuation does not discount for this currency: the factor is 1.
curves.discountDetails: Zero rate {{rate}} % a year over {{days}} days
curves.noPriceHint: No official curve covers this on or before the date.
curves.noSnapshotsHint: Build one from the day's quotes; it becomes official when a second person signs it off.

valuation.title: Valuation
valuation.description: End-of-day mark to market of {{entity}} against official curves.
valuation.noExplain: No P&L explain for these dates
valuation.officialHint: The official run on this date, or the latest one before it.
valuation.noOfficial: No official run on or before this date
valuation.noOfficialHint: Runs become official when a second person signs them off.
valuation.noExplainHint: Both dates need an official run; pick the dates of two signed-off runs.
valuation.explainHint: How the mark to market moved between the two official runs, by cause ({{currency}}).
valuation.noRuns: No valuation runs in the last 90 days
valuation.runDescription: Mark to market of every open delivery against the official curves, in {{currency}}.

kpi.waitingHint: A second person signs them off
kpi.exceptionsHint: Deliveries without a price or rate

valuation.discountHint: MtM is the undiscounted amount times the discount factor of the discount curve to the pay date. Futures are not discounted.

option.vegaHint: Option value change per volatility point, per tonne. Option rows are keyed by the leg; the delivery date is the expiry.

valuation.ctdHint: Cheapest to deliver: the average value per MWh of the certificates that would deliver the sale. Shown only; the official MtM stays on the bucket curve.

portfolio.lead: Portfolio value is a management view: the certificates held, valued at the best price each one qualifies for, plus the trades marked to market, less what it costs to deliver the open obligations from the book. Official MtM, the ledger, EMIR and credit stay on the bucket curves.
portfolio.none: Portfolio value is not available for this run
portfolio.noneHint: Only runs built with a valuation-grade allocation carry a portfolio value.
portfolio.inventoryHint: Certificates held, each at its best price
portfolio.bridgeHint: Inventory value plus trade MtM, less the cost of delivering the open obligations ({{currency}}).
portfolio.bridgeChart: Waterfall from inventory value to portfolio value
portfolio.explainTitle: Change against the prior official run
portfolio.explainHint: What moved the portfolio value since the prior official run, by cause ({{currency}}).
portfolio.explainPending: The explain against the prior official run appears once this run is official.
portfolio.noChange: No change against the prior run
portfolio.obligationsHint: Cheapest to deliver is the average value per MWh of the certificates that deliver the obligation; the sale mark is the price of the sale. Give-away is the difference.
portfolio.explainSectionHint: How the portfolio value moved between the official runs of the dates above, by cause. A management view, not the ledger.
portfolio.noExplain: No portfolio explain for these dates
portfolio.noExplainHint: Both dates need an official run with a portfolio value.
portfolio.noSteps: No official runs with a portfolio value in this period
portfolio.noStepsHint: Pick other dates, or sign off a run that carries a portfolio value.
portfolio.realisedGiveAway: Give-away handed over by plans approved in the period

risk.title: Risk
risk.description: Limits, counterparty exposure and credit support of {{entity}}.

typeHints.CREDIT_EXPOSURE: Exposure to one counterparty, in money.
typeHints.POSITION_NET: Net position of a product family, optionally of one book.
typeHints.TENOR_MAX_MONTHS: Longest tenor a trade may have, in months.
typeHints.STOP_LOSS_MTD: Loss for the month to date, in money.
typeHints.COMPLIANCE_SHORT: Allowances still missing for a compliance year, in tonnes.
typeHints.GOO_CONCENTRATION: Unsold certificates of one product bucket: held GoO that no obligation uses. Applies to the whole entity.
typeHints.GOO_EXPIRY: Held certificates that expire within the horizon and that no obligation uses. Applies to the whole entity.
typeHints.GOO_BASIS: Sales delivered with certificates worth more than their own product (the give-away). Applies to the whole entity.
typeHints.MARGIN_LIQUIDITY: Cash tied up at clearing houses: initial margin held plus margin calls still to pay, in money. Applies to the whole entity.

risk.fourEyesHint: Applies once a second person approves it in the inbox.
risk.vintageHint: Narrow the limit to certificates produced in one year (and sales marked at it)
risk.noExposures: No exposure measured yet: measure the limits or wait for the next scheduled run.
risk.noCreditSupport: No credit support with this counterparty
risk.pfeHint: Potential future exposure add-ons as a percentage of notional, by remaining tenor. Uncalibrated values are placeholders.
risk.noLimits: No limits yet; request one and have a second analyst approve it

kpi.inBreachHint: Over their amount at the last measurement

ets.description: Installations, emissions and surrender obligations of {{entity}}.
ets.name: Name
ets.accountHint: Union Registry accounts of the entity
ets.surrenderHint: Surrenders allowances for {{year}} from the installation's account through the registry.
ets.noInstallationsHint: Register an installation or aircraft operator to follow its compliance here.
ets.chartHint: Allowances held and surrendered against the year's emissions, by installation.

hedges.title: Cash flow hedges
hedges.description: Forecast allowance and certificate transactions of {{entity}} hedged by forwards, with their documentation and effectiveness.
hedges.designateIntro: Hedge accounting applies from the day a second accountant approves the designation. It is never applied to earlier valuations.
hedges.designated: Hedge {{number}} proposed; a second accountant approves it in the inbox

kpi.pendingHint: A second accountant decides in the inbox

hedges.emptyHint: A hedge links forwards you hold to a forecast purchase or sale, so their value changes are recognised in equity until the transaction happens.
hedges.emptyFilteredHint: Pick another status or show all.

form.itemHint: A highly probable purchase or sale of allowances or certificates.
form.objectiveHint: Goes into the hedge documentation, for example what is hedged, why and how effectiveness is judged.
form.instrumentsHint: Open fixed-price forwards of this entity on the {{side}} side. A trade can be designated at most in full across open hedges.
form.noTrades: No open {{side}} trades of this product family
form.fourEyes: A second accountant approves the designation in the inbox before it takes effect.

detail.checksHint: Critical terms of the instruments and the hedged item. They inform the decision; they do not block it.

measurements.title: Measurements
measurements.chartHint: Change in the instruments' value since designation, the hypothetical derivative's value and the reserve, in {{currency}}, on each official valuation.
measurements.emptyHint: A hedge is measured on every official valuation signed off after its designation. Earlier valuations are not measured, so the first measurement comes with the next official valuation.
measurements.method: The reserve is the lower of the instruments' change and the hypothetical derivative's value when both move the same way; the rest is ineffectiveness in profit or loss.

discontinuation.title: Discontinuation
discontinuation.stillExpected: Still expected: the reserve is frozen at its last measured amount
discontinuation.notExpected: No longer expected: the reserve is recycled to profit or loss
discontinuation.waiting: Waiting for a second accountant to approve.

discontinue.title: Discontinue hedge {{number}}
discontinue.intro: Hedge accounting stops once a second accountant approves. Say whether the forecast transaction is still expected.
discontinue.stillExpected: The forecast transaction is still expected
discontinue.stillExpectedHint: On: the reserve is frozen at its last measured amount until the transaction happens. Off: it is recycled to profit or loss.
discontinue.requested: Discontinuation of {{number}} requested; a second accountant approves it in the inbox

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.description: Journal, trial balance, chart of accounts and posting rules of {{entity}}.
ledger.chainIntact: The hash chain of the journal is intact.
ledger.chainBroken: The hash chain is broken: tell the administrator.
ledger.balanceHint: Debits must equal credits; the server checks.
ledger.ruleFourEyes: The rule changes once a second accountant approves it in the inbox.
ledger.conditionsHint: A JSON object of event attributes that must match, for example {"movementType": "PURCHASE"}
ledger.ruleAmountHint: Each line names the event amount it posts, for example amount or cost.
ledger.ruleSidesHint: A rule needs at least one debit and one credit line.

kpi.accountsHint: Chart of accounts of the entity

monthEnd.title: Month end
monthEnd.description: Close the books of {{entity}}: period end, GL interface and accounting policies.
monthEnd.hardClosed: Hard-closed: correct in an open period.
monthEnd.noRuns: No period-end run for this period yet
monthEnd.importHint: Paste the GL trial balance: one account per line as account;balance;currency (comma or tab also work).
monthEnd.glRestricted: The GL interface is for accountants and auditors.
monthEnd.csvExported: Export generated and saved as a file

next.OPEN: Run period end, then soft close
next.SOFT_CLOSED: Export to the GL, then hard close

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: Reports for your roles; every run is numbered and its content hashed ({{entity}}).
reports.emirUnverified: {{count}} EMIR field rules are not yet checked against the regulatory technical standards.
reports.reportErrorHint: Records an EROR event for the trade, for example after the trade repository rejected it. It cannot be undone.
reports.notRunHint: Fill in the parameters and run the report; every run is numbered and its content hashed.

admin.referenceDescription: Legal entities, counterparties, registries and production devices. Every change is versioned.
admin.fourEyesNote: Registry integration modes, counterparty registry accounts and bank accounts change only with a second person's approval in the inbox.
admin.taxonomyDescription: Code sets for devices, criteria and buckets. Nodes are versioned and retired by an end date, never deleted.
admin.countriesHint: ISO country codes, two letters each
admin.productsDescription: Buckets decide which certificates count for which position; allowance products and futures contracts.
admin.bucketCriterionFixed: The criterion stays as defined ({{summary}}); retire the bucket and create a new one to change it.
admin.changeRequestsDescription: Sensitive master data changes waiting for, or decided by, a second person.
admin.accountingPolicyNote: The accounting policy changes through month end, approved by a second person.
admin.counterpartySensitiveNote: Registry and bank accounts change through requests a second person approves; credit limits are risk limits.
admin.blankKeeps: A cleared field keeps its stored value.
admin.obligationsOpenAt: Delivery obligations open when a trade is
admin.deviceIdentityFixed: GSRN, location, technology and owner are fixed once a device exists.
admin.gsrnHint: 18 digits, the last a GS1 check digit
admin.gsrnInvalid: The check digit does not match
admin.asOfHint: The record as it was known at this time
admin.noRecordAsOf: The record did not exist at that time.
admin.noRequestsHint: Changes to registry integration, counterparty registry accounts and bank accounts are requested from reference data and appear here until a second person decides.
admin.issuanceLagHint: Days from the end of a production month until the registry issues its certificates.

forecast.title: Production forecast
forecast.lead: Expected production of the next twelve months. A month without a forecast uses the technology's load factor times the capacity, which is only an estimate.
forecast.lag: Certificates are issued {{days}} days after the month ends.
forecast.expectedHint: Whole MWh the device is expected to produce (P50).
forecast.p90Hint: Whole MWh the device should reach in nine cases out of ten; not above the expected figure.
forecast.fallbackHint: No forecast is recorded for this month. The figure is the capacity times the technology's load factor.
forecast.editFallbackHint: Saving records a forecast for this month and replaces the load-factor estimate.
forecast.p90Above: A whole number, not above the expected figure
forecast.emptyHint: The device is not in operation in the coming twelve months.
forecast.importHint: A CSV file with a header line and one line per device and month: gsrn,month,expected_mwh,p90_mwh, with the month like 2026-11. Lines that fail are skipped and listed.

loadFactors.title: Load factors
loadFactors.lead: The share of capacity each technology produces in a month, used where no forecast is recorded. They are illustrative defaults, not measurements. Each cell shows the expected factor with the P90 factor beneath it.
loadFactors.edit: Edit the load factor of {{technology}} in {{month}}
loadFactors.factorHint: Between 0 and 1: the share of the capacity produced over the month.
loadFactors.invalidP90: A number between 0 and the factor

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.description: Every domain event and command, append-only and hash-chained. Filters live in the URL.
audit.emptyFiltered: No event matches these filters. Widen the dates or clear a filter.
audit.emptyHint: Commands and domain events appear here as they are recorded.
audit.sameRecord: Show every event of this record

palette.placeholder: Go to a screen, find a trade by number, reference or UTI, or search the help

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.description: Deliveries to invoice and invoices of {{entity}}
settlement.priceFixed: Price fixed; the items were evaluated again
settlement.itemResolved: The item is open for invoicing
settlement.runHint: Drafts one sales invoice per counterparty and currency for open items delivered up to the date. Drafts are submitted for a second person's approval.
settlement.purchaseHint: A supplier's invoice is matched to our open purchases from that supplier; net and VAT must agree with them within 0.05. It is issued after a second person approves it.
settlement.noOpenPurchases: No open purchases from this supplier in this currency
settlement.chooseSupplier: Choose the supplier to see its open purchases
settlement.purchaseRegistered: Purchase invoice registered as a draft
settlement.amountsHint: Amounts and VAT are computed by the server from the deliveries and the approved VAT rules.
settlement.frozenAtIssue: Details are frozen from reference data when the invoice is issued
settlement.discardHint: Its deliveries become open again and can be invoiced later.
settlement.creditNoteHint: Drafts a credit note that reverses the invoice in full. It is issued after a second person approves it.
settlement.allocateAmountHint: Empty: as much as the invoice still owes
settlement.bankReferenceHint: Recording the same reference again returns the earlier payment
settlement.cancelNettingHint: The invoices stay open and can be netted or paid again.
settlement.counterpartyRefHint: How the counterparty confirmed the statement, e.g. their e-mail or document number
settlement.importPaymentsHint: One payment per line: bank_reference,value_date,amount,currency[,counterparty,remittance]. A negative amount is a payment we made. Lines imported before are skipped.
settlement.legalTextHint: Printed on invoices, e.g. the reverse-charge reference
settlement.netPaymentHint: An unapplied payment of {{amount}} with this counterparty

nettingDirections.even: The invoices offset exactly; nothing is paid

settlement.nettingSettled: Netting settled; the invoices are paid
settlement.nettingValueDateHint: Invoices due by this date are netted
settlement.noIntraEuSales: No sales to businesses in other member states in this period
settlement.noNetPayment: No unapplied payment fits; record the payment first
settlement.noOpenInvoices: No open invoices fit this payment
settlement.nothingIssued: No invoices issued in this period
settlement.nothingToPay: Nothing is paid: the invoices offset exactly.
settlement.ownNetting: You prepared this statement, so someone else records the counterparty's agreement.
settlement.paysInvoicesHint: Empty: invoice numbers found in the remittance text are paid; the rest stays unapplied
settlement.prepareNettingHint: Nets every issued, unpaid invoice with the counterparty in the currency, due by the value date. The counterparty's agreement is recorded by another person.
settlement.proposeRuleHint: A new rule, or a new version of an existing code. It applies only after another accountant approves it in the inbox; items waiting for it are evaluated again then.
settlement.recordPaymentHint: A payment from the bank. It is applied to the invoices you choose, or to invoice numbers in the remittance text.

noItems.attention: Nothing needs attention: every delivery is priced and has a VAT rule
noItems.open: No open items: every delivery is invoiced
noItems.all: No settlement items yet; they appear when deliveries are recorded

kpi.attentionHint: Fix the price or evaluate again

registry.title: Registry
registry.description: Registry instructions of {{entity}}, transfer routes and statement formats
registry.transferHint: Moves certificates to another account. A part of a lot is split off first. The transfer waits for a second person's approval in the inbox before it is sent.
registry.noRoute: No route on record between these registries; the registry decides whether it can be done.
registry.routeFeasible: Route available: fee {{fee}} per MWh, about {{days}} days
registry.routeInfeasible: These registries cannot transfer to each other.
registry.transferSubmitted: Transfer submitted; it waits for approval
registry.routesHint: Used by the allocation engine to score sources, and shown before manual transfers.
registry.formatsHint: How each registry's statement and transaction exports are read.
registry.cancelHint: A lot in transfer is released; reserved allowances are given back.
registry.failHint: The registry refused the instruction or it cannot be completed. It can be retried or cancelled afterwards.
registry.confirmHint: Record this only when the registry shows the transaction as completed.
registry.formatEditorHint: The column mapping names the column header for each statement field; the server checks the fields against the kind. Registry * makes a profile usable for every registry.
registry.cancellationHint: Cancels the certificates in the registry for a beneficiary. The instruction waits for a second person's approval in the inbox; the lot leaves our books when the registry confirms it.
registry.cancellationSubmitted: Cancellation submitted; it waits for approval
registry.beneficiaryIdHint: Optional, e.g. a business ID or metering point
registry.allowanceTransferHint: Moves allowances to another account in the same registry. They are reserved at once; the transfer waits for a second person's approval and is then carried out in the registry.
registry.allowanceTransferSubmitted: Allowance transfer submitted; it waits for approval
registry.noFreeAllowances: This account has no free allowances.

kpi.openHint: Not yet confirmed by the registry
kpi.pendingHint: A second person decides in the inbox
kpi.attentionHint: Failed, or the outcome is unknown

registry.emptyHint: Transfers, cancellations and surrenders appear here once they are submitted.
registry.relatedTasksHint: The approval and any follow-up in the inbox.

clearing.title: Clearing
clearing.description: Daily margin of the EUA futures of {{entity}} at its clearing houses, against the clearing member's statements
clearing.accountsHint: A clearing account is one entity at one clearing house, through a clearing member. Its cleared EUA futures are margined every business day. Choose a row to work on that account in the other tabs.
clearing.newAccountHint: Opens a clearing account for {{entity}}. Its futures with the clearing house as counterparty are margined from the next business day computed.
clearing.noClearingHouses: No clearing house in the counterparties
clearing.noAccountsHint: Create an account for {{entity}} and its cleared EUA futures are margined every business day.

fields.codeHint: A short name, unique among the accounts
fields.clearingMemberHint: The bank or broker the account is held through
fields.currencyHint: Trades in another currency are refused, not converted

clearing.chooseAccountHint: Create a clearing account on the Accounts tab first.
clearing.rangeInvalid: The period ends before it starts
clearing.marginHint: The margin we compute for each business day from positions, trades and the official settlement prices. A run never changes: new inputs supersede it with the next version, and only the current version of each day is listed.
clearing.computeMarginHint: Computes the variation margin of {{account}} for one business day. The same inputs again return the current run; changed inputs (an amended trade, a corrected price) supersede it. A missing settlement price stops the day.
clearing.noRuns: No margin runs in this period
clearing.noRunsHint: Runs are computed every weekday evening, or by hand with Compute margin.
clearing.runHint: Variation margin per contract: the position carried over moves with the change in settlement price, and trades of the day settle against their price.
clearing.runSuperseded: A later version replaced this run at {{at}}.
clearing.importHint: The clearing member's statement for {{account}}, as CSV with one or more days. Each day is stored as a version and compared with our margin; a difference opens a break.
clearing.importResult: {{imported}} new versions stored, {{unchanged}} unchanged, {{breaks}} open breaks
clearing.statementsHint: What the clearing member says was paid, one statement per business day. The current version of each day is listed; the same figures again change nothing.
clearing.noStatementsHint: Import the member's statement to compare it with the margin we computed.
clearing.statementHint: The member's figures for the day. The initial margin of the latest day sets the level held; fees are charged to the books.
clearing.statementSuperseded: A later version replaced this statement at {{at}}.
clearing.breaksHint: A break is a day on which the member's statement differs from our margin. It closes when a correction makes the two agree, or when a second person accepts the member's figures in the inbox.
clearing.noBreaksHint: Breaks appear when an imported statement differs from the margin we computed.

differenceHints.NO_RUN: The member sent a statement for a day we have no margin run for.
differenceHints.POSITION: The position after the day differs.
differenceHints.VARIATION_MARGIN: The margin paid for the contract differs.
differenceHints.SETTLEMENT_PRICE: The settlement price the member used differs from the official one.

clearing.breakNextTask: A second person accepts the member's figures with a reason in the inbox, or the break closes by itself when a correction makes the margin agree.
clearing.breakNext: The break closes when a correction makes the margin agree, or when a second person accepts the member's figures in the inbox.
clearing.differencesHint: Ours is the margin run, theirs the member's statement. A contract missing on one side is flat with no margin.
clearing.noDifferences: No differences are left on this break.
clearing.callsHint: A call opens when the cash at the member is below the initial margin required; the amount is the shortfall. It is paid or disputed in the inbox by a second person.
clearing.noCallsHint: Calls open when an imported statement shows less cash at the member than the initial margin.
clearing.callHint: The shortfall of cash at the member against the initial margin, from the latest statement.

reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
reconciliation.description: Registry statements against the books of {{entity}}

types.MISSING_INTERNALLY: In the registry, not in our books
types.MISSING_IN_REGISTRY: In our books, not in the registry

reconciliation.subject: Certificates or balance
reconciliation.uploadHoldingsHint: The account's holdings as the registry exports them. It is read with the registry's statement format, then reconciled at once: new differences become breaks, and breaks the registry no longer shows clear themselves.
reconciliation.uploadTransactionsHint: A registry's transaction export: open instructions it shows as completed are confirmed, failed ones are failed. It affects every legal entity, so it needs access to all of them.
reconciliation.transactionResult: {{lines}} lines: {{confirmed}} confirmed, {{failed}} failed, {{final}} already final, {{unmatched}} unmatched
reconciliation.noBreaks: No breaks: the registry agrees with our books.

typeHints.MISSING_INTERNALLY: The registry shows certificates we have no lot for: record them as received, or accept the difference.
typeHints.MISSING_IN_REGISTRY: We hold certificates the registry no longer shows: confirm the transfer that took them, withdraw our lot, or accept the difference.
typeHints.ATTRIBUTE_MISMATCH: Our lot describes the certificates differently: correct the correctable fields, replace the lot with the registry's version, or accept the difference.
typeHints.BALANCE_MISMATCH: Our allowance balance differs from the registry's: book the difference as a correction, or accept it.

reconciliation.awaitingAcceptance: {{by}} asked to accept this break as it is; another person decides in the inbox.
reconciliation.confirmInstructionHint: The registry executed the transfer that holds these certificates; it is confirmed and the lot leaves our books.
reconciliation.withdrawHint: The certificates are no longer ours in the registry; the missing range is split off and withdrawn.
reconciliation.correctHoldingHint: Books the difference between the registry's balance and ours as a correction movement.
reconciliation.acceptHint: The difference stays in our books as it is, with your reason. A second person approves it in the inbox.
reconciliation.acceptanceRequested: Acceptance requested; it waits for a second person
reconciliation.receiptHint: The certificates as the registry shows them become a lot of ours on this account.
reconciliation.replaceHint: Our lot is withdrawn and replaced by a lot with the registry's attributes.
reconciliation.notReconciled: This statement has been imported but not reconciled yet.
reconciliation.noBreaksHint: A break appears when a registry statement differs from our books.
reconciliation.noStatements: No statements for this account yet
reconciliation.detailsHint: The differences the reconciliation recorded for this break.

confirmations.title: Confirmations
confirmations.description: Counterparty confirmations of {{entity}}'s trades, matched against ours
confirmations.hint: A confirmation that differs from ours opens a task: a second middle or back office user overrides it (the trade is confirmed) or disputes it.
confirmations.uploadHint: One line per delivery: confirmation_ref, our_trade_ref or counterparty_trade_ref, trade_date, product_family, product, quantity, unit, price, currency, delivery_date, and optionally amount, payment_date, seller_name, buyer_name, seller_lei, buyer_lei, seller_account, buyer_account. Lines with the same confirmation_ref form one confirmation.
confirmations.enterHint: Starts from our terms. Enter what the counterparty's confirmation states; it is matched against ours when you save it.

received.MISMATCHED: Received; it differs from ours and waits for a decision
received.RECEIVED: Received; it is matched when ours is issued

confirmations.mismatchHint: Their terms differ from ours. A second person overrides the differences (the trade is confirmed) or disputes the confirmation in the inbox.

kpi.mismatchedHint: Waiting for a second person's decision

confirmations.emptyHint: Counterparty confirmations arrive by CSV upload or are entered on the trade.
confirmations.comparisonHint: Field by field, with the matcher's verdict on each.
confirmations.termsHint: The terms as we issued them.

login.tagline: Guarantees of Origin and EU ETS allowances, from trade to ledger
login.title: Sign in to the demo
login.expired: Your session ended. Sign in again to continue.
login.aboutPersonas: After signing in you act as one of the personas (trader, middle office, back office, accountant, risk, auditor, admin) and can switch at any time from the top right. Approvals need a second person, so switch to the second persona of the same role to approve.
login.aboutShared: The data is shared: other visitors see what you change.
login.aboutReset: Everything is reset to the example portfolio every night.
login.aboutFictitious: All companies, counterparties, devices, registries and prices are fictitious.
login.access: Ask the person who shared this demo with you for the sign-in details.

demoSeed.title: Preparing the demo data
demoSeed.text: The example portfolio is being created through the application's own API. This takes a minute or two after a start or a reset.

demo.title: Demo
demo.description: The public demo's example portfolio: when it was created and when it is reset.
demo.resetExplain: The application restarts and rebuilds the example portfolio from scratch. Everything visitors changed is lost, and everyone has to sign in again. It takes a minute or two.
demo.resetHint: You return to the sign-in page when the new data is ready.
demo.cooling: The demo started recently; a reset is possible from {{at}}.
demo.notShowcase: Only the public demo (showcase profile) can be reset. Here, drop the database to start over.
